################################################################################################################################
#SAMPLE CODE
################################################################################################################################
generate.correlation.matrix<-function(M,ncases=1000) {
  if (missing(M))
    M=matrix(c(1,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,1,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,1,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,1,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,1,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,1,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,1),nrow=7,ncol=7)
  L=chol(M)
  nvars=dim(L)[1]
  t(L)%*%L
  r=t(L)%*%matrix(rnorm(nvars*ncases),nrow=nvars,ncol=ncases)
  r=data.frame(t(r))
  return(r)
}
rn<-generate.correlation.matrix()
library(mirt)
mirtCluster()
bfactor<-mirt::bfactor(data=rn,model=c(1,1,1,2,2,2,2),technical=list(NCYCLES=20000,MAXQUAD=80000,parallel=TRUE))
coef(bfactor)
################################################################################################################################

I was trying to get the parameters of a bifactor model. And naturally I used coef(object), which returned "Error: $ operator not defined for this S4 class"
So I got curious I tried coef with a single factor mirt model and coef() worked. However it seems that coef also does not work with multidimensional models such as graded partial credit etc created with the mirt() function.
The model above will have some convergence issues however, even if the model converges I get the same error.
I have also noticed that it is possible however to generate scores for models which do not display coef(). 
I wonder if there is any way to get the coefficients of a multidimensional object created with mirt or bifactor functions.
To me all these are very strange. Does anyone have an opinion on the issue?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: coef(object) of a bifactor model returns Error: $ operator not defined for this S4 class
parts:
Your data is continuous, while mirt should only be used for categorical items (typically with less than 10 categories, but more commonly from 2-7). The reason this fails to converge is because it's not identified. Use something like the lavaan package for this simulation because it is designed for continuous data. 

Phil

parts:
Because they don't have to be ordinal. They can be nominal.

Phil
On Tue, Aug 30, 2016 at 12:05 PM, Dimitrios Zacharatos <sedz...@gmail.com> wrote:

But you can use ordinal data with your package as well. Why you prefer the term categorical over ordinal?

On Tuesday, August 30, 2016 at 6:58:53 PM UTC+3, Phil Chalmers wrote:
"mirt" as in the package, not the function. That's fine, just so long as the data are categorical then all estimation functions in mirt (the package) will work fine.

Phil

On Tue, Aug 30, 2016 at 11:57 AM, Dimitrios Zacharatos <sedz...@gmail.com> wrote:
oh. I din't use mirt I used bfactor. Does bfactor work with ordinal data? Because I don't know what happened but my model converges and works. Obvioulsy the simulation I did is a on the fly simulation just to illustrate the point (wrongly obviously). My real data are ordinal and I used bfactor. You scared me now.

On Tuesday, August 30, 2016 at 6:40:16 PM UTC+3, Phil Chalmers wrote:
Your data is continuous, while mirt should only be used for categorical items (typically with less than 10 categories, but more commonly from 2-7). The reason this fails to converge is because it's not identified. Use something like the lavaan package for this simulation because it is designed for continuous data. 

Phil

On Tue, Aug 30, 2016 at 11:29 AM, Dimitrios Zacharatos <sedz...@gmail.com> wrote:
and I still have no idea what "Error: $ operator not defined for this S4 class" means
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/36737628/error-operator-not-defined-for-this-s4-class

On Tuesday, August 30, 2016 at 6:17:40 PM UTC+3, Dimitrios Zacharatos wrote:
################################################################################################################################
#SAMPLE CODE
################################################################################################################################
generate.correlation.matrix<-function(M,ncases=1000) {
  if (missing(M))
    M=matrix(c(1,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,1,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,1,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,1,0.9,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,1,0.9,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,1,0.9,
               0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,0.9,1),nrow=7,ncol=7)
  L=chol(M)
  nvars=dim(L)[1]
  t(L)%*%L
  r=t(L)%*%matrix(rnorm(nvars*ncases),nrow=nvars,ncol=ncases)
  r=data.frame(t(r))
  return(r)
}
rn<-generate.correlation.matrix()
library(mirt)
mirtCluster()
bfactor<-mirt::bfactor(data=rn,model=c(1,1,1,2,2,2,2),technical=list(NCYCLES=20000,MAXQUAD=80000,parallel=TRUE))
coef(bfactor)
################################################################################################################################

I was trying to get the parameters of a bifactor model. And naturally I used coef(object), which returned "Error: $ operator not defined for this S4 class"
So I got curious I tried coef with a single factor mirt model and coef() worked. However it seems that coef also does not work with multidimensional models such as graded partial credit etc created with the mirt() function.
The model above will have some convergence issues however, even if the model converges I get the same error.
I have also noticed that it is possible however to generate scores for models which do not display coef(). 
I wonder if there is any way to get the coefficients of a multidimensional object created with mirt or bifactor functions.
To me all these are very strange. Does anyone have an opinion on the issue?
